_comment: Budgets of the guardrails H1-H10 (target design §6), checked by .github/scripts/structure_budget.py. They only go down: lower a value when a change improves it; raising one needs the code owners review. H10 values are line counts that only warn.

_detached_allow_list.reason: The TLS handshake of an accepted connection, then its delivery: listed in the listener's pending handshakes until it ends, bounded by the handshake deadline; stop() closes it and waits for its delivery.
An in-memory dispatch with a callback: ends within the dispatch timeout (its handler may go on, counted apart), then calls the callback once.
The writer of the connection: one write at a time (writing_), holding the connection until it returns the turn.
The graceful close of a lingering connection: holds it, bounded by the linger byte limit and timeout.
The read loop of an SSE stream: holds it and ends when the client goes or the stream stops; it owns the stream.
The read loop of a WebSocket connection: holds it, ends when it closes or is released, and breaks the callback cycles when it ends.
The closing handshake of a WebSocket connection: holds it, bounded by the websocket's CLOSE_TIMEOUT, and wakes its reader when it ends.
The writer of a push connection's queue (WebSocket, SSE): one at a time (writing_), holding its owner until the queue is empty or closed.
The writer of the control frames queued during a write: holds the websocket, which keeps the write turn until they are sent.
The closing handshake once the websocket closed: owns its socket, bounded by CLOSE_TIMEOUT.
The loop of a socket pipe: holds it and ends when either socket ends or cancel() is called, closing both.
The loop of an upgraded proxy tunnel: owns both sockets and ends when either one closes.
The message loop of a WebSocket client (run()): ends when reading fails; stop() and the destructor close the connection.
